keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Republic of Vietnam shape for 1967-1972 (its rows run 1956-1966 and 1973-1975), although the state held Saigon and its provinces throughout: 'Second Republic established: 1 April 1967'. The Viet Cong zones of these years (1968: 'about one-fifth of the people who lived in southern Vietnam' in 'areas that were controlled by Viet Cong') are carried by the 1961 contest, not by a cut in the shape. Cliopatria's United States of America row (1967-2005) overlaps this land: see notes.

168,922 km2 for 1973-1975 against the infobox's 173,809 km2 (ratio 0.97). The shape is the 1966 shape minus 43 cells (about 10,900 km2, 13.8-17.0 N, 106.7-107.8 E) in the north and the western highlands, which fits the PRG's capital at Cam Lo (Quang Tri) from 1973 and the page's 'PAVN forces in the South were permitted to remain in place', but neither page gives a zone boundary: unverified: page budget. The ledger carries the cut as a hatched occupation, as the democratic-republic-of-vietnam dossier does.

ledger.note: 1961: the Viet Cong hold half the countryside south and southwest of Saigon. The page dates the National Liberation Front to 20 December 1960 (infobox; 'led in 1959 to the foundation of the National Front') and says 'one-half of the entire rural region south and southwest of Saigon' was under considerable Communist control in 1961; the NLF's government from 8 June 1969 is the PRG, whose slug stands for the whole movement.
1967: the Second Republic is established (1 April, infobox); the state, its colour and its land continue under President Nguyễn Văn Thiệu.

ledger.note: 1973: the Paris Peace Accords (27 January) leave the communist forces in their zones. 'US military forces withdrew from South Vietnam at the end of March 1973 while PAVN forces in the South were permitted to remain in place.' The PRG page: it 'signed the 1973 Paris Peace Treaty as an independent entity' and its capital was Cam Lộ from 1973. The extent is Cliopatria's cut (confidence 2: the year is the pages', the zone is the shape's); the democratic-republic-of-vietnam dossier records the PAVN side.

region.text: 'the Republic of Vietnam also administered parts of the Paracels and Spratly Islands'; 'China seized control of the Paracels in 1974 after the South Vietnamese navy attempted an assault on PRC-claimed islands'

ledger.note: 1974: China seizes the Paracels from South Vietnam. The page gives the year and the land ('the Paracels') but not the month or which islands the Republic held ('parts of'); the Cliopatria shape never included them, so the event removes no drawn cells. Reviewer se-04-b (2026-10-20): month 1 from the page's 'The same month, China attacked South Vietnamese forces in the Paracel Islands, taking control of the islands', which follows the 4 January 1974 statement that the war had restarted.

wars.name: Vietnam War

zones.text: the Viet Cong countryside south and southwest of Saigon from 1961

wars.outcome: The communist side won: Saigon fell on 30 April 1975 and the Republic ended; the PRG and North Vietnam merged into the Socialist Republic of Vietnam on 2 July 1976.
wars.note: The page gives no start date for the war: the NLF is dated 20 December 1960, the Tet Offensive 31 January 1968 ('the PAVN and the Viet Cong broke the traditional truce'), the Easter Offensive 'late March 1972', the Paris Peace Accords 27 January 1973 and 'a major combined-arms conventional invasion in 1975'. Contested provinces year by year are not on the page (se-04-x).

notes: Wikidata Q172640 is shared with the Democratic Republic of Vietnam; the two are different states (separate articles, South Vietnam and North Vietnam; opposing governments), so there is no merge; this dossier keeps the Republic of Vietnam under its own slug. The state begins on 26 October 1955, the republic's proclamation: the State of Vietnam (1949-1955, 'withdrew from the French Union on July 20, 1954') is the same state under Bảo Đại and has no Cliopatria row (Cliopatria draws French Indochina over the south to 1955). It is not given a dossier of its own; a gap-filler may extend the start back to 1949 or 26 June 1954 once a page dates the transfer of the south from French administration (the page does not mention Cochinchina, the 1954 transfer of provinces or the French withdrawal of 1956). Cliopatria has no shape for 1967-1972 (new keyframe 1967 fills it with the 1966 shape). The Viet Cong, NLF (20 December 1960) and PRG (8 June 1969) are one movement that held land and needs a dossier of type rebel (suggested slug provisional-revolutionary-government-of-the-republic-of-south-vietnam, 1960-1976, capitals Tay Ninh, Loc Ninh, Cam Lo, Saigon-Gia Dinh); this dossier's contest and 1973 occupation events point at it and at the democratic-republic-of-vietnam. Page budget (1-2) was spent on the South Vietnam and PRG articles; the PRG article gives no territory, so the 1973 shape is unverified beyond the PRG capital at Cam Lo, and the contested provinces of the war year by year, the Easter Offensive's front (Quang Tri) and the Paracel battle's month are left to the group's additions batch and a gap-filler. Cliopatria's French Indochina row has a 1956-1957 shape of 35,422 km2 that the gazetteer places at 55-168 E, 20-50 S (not in Indochina): another group's row to look at. The Spratly islands held by the Republic are named on the page ('parts of the Paracels and Spratly Islands') but no loss is dated, so only the Paracels are in the ledger. The Paracel loss resolves to no land cells (islands are off the grid), so it is a record, not a drawn change. Cliopatria's United States of America shape for 1967-2005 contains 551 cells (139,348 km2) that are the Republic's 1966 land and, after 1975, the Socialist Republic's south (the seed lists the United States as a neighbour of this state in 1973-1975): no page opened here records a US occupation, so the overlap is a fault in that row for the am-07 group, and it may be why Cliopatria has no Republic shape in 1967-1972.
